title: Netlify — Jamstack Hosting
subtitle: Deploy static sites and SPAs with git-based CI/CD, form handling, identity, and edge functions

content.text: Netlify and Vercel are very similar — both deploy frontend apps with git integration, preview deployments, custom domains, and serverless functions. Netlify pioneered many of these features (it invented the term 'Jamstack'). The key differences: Netlify has built-in form handling (collect form submissions without a backend), identity (authentication), and split testing out of the box. Vercel is better for Next.js and has a faster CDN. For non-Next.js static sites, either works equally well.

content.code:
# Install Netlify CLI
npm install -g netlify-cli

# Login and deploy
netlify login
netlify init      # link to GitHub repo and configure
netlify deploy    # preview deploy
netlify deploy --prod  # production deploy

# Manual deploy without CLI:
# netlify.com → New site → Import from Git → Select repo
# Configure: Build command, Publish directory
# Common framework settings:
#   React/Vite:   build: npm run build, publish: dist
#   Next.js:      build: npm run build, publish: .next (with @netlify/next plugin)
#   Astro:        build: npm run build, publish: dist
#   Hugo:         build: hugo, publish: public

[build]
  command = "npm run build"
  publish = "dist"

# SPA routing — serve index.html for all routes
[[redirects]]
  from = "/*"
  to = "/index.html"
  status = 200

# 301 redirect old URLs
[[redirects]]
  from = "/old-page"
  to = "/new-page"
  status = 301

# Proxy API calls (avoid CORS issues in development)
[[redirects]]
  from = "/api/*"
  to = "https://api.myapp.com/:splat"
  status = 200
  force = true

# HTTP security headers
[[headers]]
  for = "/*"
  [headers.values]
    X-Frame-Options = "DENY"
    X-Content-Type-Options = "nosniff"
    Strict-Transport-Security = "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"

# Cache static assets long-term
[[headers]]
  for = "/assets/*"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

# Environment-specific build settings
[context.production]
  command = "npm run build:prod"

[context.branch-deploy]
  command = "npm run build:staging"

<!-- Add data-netlify='true' to any form — Netlify handles submissions -->
<form name="contact" method="POST" data-netlify="true">
  <input type="hidden" name="form-name" value="contact" />
  <label>Name: <input type="text" name="name" required /></label>
  <label>Email: <input type="email" name="email" required /></label>
  <label>Message: <textarea name="message"></textarea></label>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>

<!-- That's it! Netlify:
  - Intercepts form submissions
  - Stores them in Netlify's form dashboard
  - Sends email notifications
  - Includes spam filtering
  - Free up to 100 submissions/month
-->

content.text: The _redirects file is the quickest way to configure SPA routing. Create a file named _redirects in your public/ folder (or wherever your publish directory is) with one line: /* /index.html 200. This tells Netlify to serve index.html for any path that doesn't match a real file — exactly what React Router and Vue Router need.

questions.question: You deploy a React SPA to Netlify but navigating to '/dashboard' directly (or refreshing the page) returns a 404. What's missing?
options: You need to add a redirect rule: '/* /index.html 200' — Netlify doesn't know React Router routes; the browser needs to load index.html first
The React build output is wrong
You need to enable SPA mode in the Netlify dashboard
questions.explanation: Netlify serves static files — when you request '/dashboard', it looks for a file called 'dashboard.html' (or dashboard/index.html) and finds nothing, returning 404. React Router handles routing in JavaScript, but JavaScript only runs after index.html loads. The fix: tell Netlify to serve index.html for all paths that don't match a real file. Add '/* /index.html 200' to _redirects or netlify.toml. The '200' status (not 301) means it's a rewrite, not a redirect — the URL stays as '/dashboard'.

faq.q: Vercel vs Netlify — which should I choose?
faq.a: Both are excellent — you can't go wrong with either. Prefer Vercel for: Next.js apps (Vercel made it), better edge performance, faster deployments. Prefer Netlify for: built-in form handling, split testing, identity management, or if you prefer their dashboard UX. For a static React app with no Next.js, flip a coin — both have generous free tiers and nearly identical DX.

examples: Netlify hosts the official React documentation (react.dev uses a successor but was on Netlify for years), numerous open-source project docs, and millions of personal and business sites
Netlify's form handling has saved thousands of agency projects from needing a backend just for a contact form — many small business sites have zero backend thanks to this feature
